records.label: PQC Today v4.99.0, release notes (2026-09-19)
Throughput and latency under peak load stay within the service objectives (handshakes, signing, KMS/HSM calls).
Relying parties validate the new certificate chain (including any composite or related-certificate format chosen).
Revocation (CRL or OCSP) works for the new certificates, and response sizes stay within limits.
Certificate rollover: old and new chains are both accepted during the overlap and the old one is retired on schedule.
Downgrade to classical is refused unless policy allows it for that peer, and every allowed fallback is logged.
A peer without the target algorithm fails in the expected, logged way (no silent fallback).
Each client and server pair completes the handshake with the target algorithm or hybrid group.
Key backup, restore and recovery work for the new key types in the KMS or HSM.
Rekey: applications that look keys up by alias keep working, and anything that stored the old key identifier is found and updated.
Monitoring shows which algorithm each connection and signature used, so the migration can be measured.
Rollback to the previous configuration is tested separately from algorithm downgrade, with a named owner.
Larger keys, signatures and certificates fit every buffer, database column, message and MTU on the path.
HelloRetryRequest: a mutually supported group the client sent no key share for is negotiated after one retry.
No common group: the handshake fails with handshake_failure, and the failure is visible in monitoring.
